{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA",
    "Given unequal group sizes (Combined n=48846, ICMS Only n=11378, Dim Visual Only n=9603, Sham n=3505, Bright Visual Only n=3323), use Type III sums of squares",
    "Consider Welch's ANOVA or heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors if variance homogeneity is violated",
    "Report partial eta-squared or omega-squared for effect size estimates"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "Apply Tukey's HSD for pairwise comparisons if ANOVA assumptions are met and group variances are approximately equal",
    "If variance homogeneity is violated, use Games-Howell post-hoc test which does not assume equal variances",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use pairwise chi-square tests with Bonferroni correction or logistic regression with planned contrasts",
    "Focus comparisons on Combined vs. single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and all conditions vs. Sham",
    "Examine whether Combined stimulation shows additive or synergistic effects relative to unimodal conditions"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control for the 10 pairwise comparisons per response variable (family-wise error rate controlled at alpha=0.05); given large sample sizes, also report Bonferroni-corrected p-values for conservative interpretation; for the five response variables, apply hierarchical testing with Success and Time-to-Target as primary endpoints",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression is recommended as the primary predictive model because Stim Paradigm is a categorical response with 5 unordered levels. The model would predict stimulation paradigm membership from the five performance variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD). Alternative: ordinal logistic regression if a theoretical ordering exists (e.g., Sham < single-modality < Combined), though this requires validation. Random forest or gradient boosting machines could serve as ensemble benchmarks given the large sample size and potential nonlinear relationships. Avoid ordinary linear regression as it inappropriately treats the categorical response as continuous. For interpretability, report multinomial log-odds coefficients, confusion matrix, and classification accuracy with 5-fold cross-validation stratified by Stim Paradigm to handle class imbalance (Combined comprises 63.7% of observations).",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check normality of residuals for continuous variables using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on subsamples (given n=76655, formal tests will likely reject; focus on visual inspection and robustness)",
    "Assess homogeneity of variances using Levene's test; given large group size disparities, expect violations and plan Welch corrections",
    "Examine independence assumption via mixed-effects models with Mouse as random effect (8 mice, repeated measures); if intraclass correlation is substantial, use linear mixed models instead of ANOVA",
    "Check for multicollinearity among predictors in multinomial logistic regression (VIF < 5)",
    "Verify complete separation or quasi-complete separation in logistic components (Firth's penalized logistic regression if needed)",
    "Assess model fit via likelihood ratio tests, AIC/BIC, and pseudo-R-squared measures"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows fastest Time-to-Target and highest Success rate compared to unimodal conditions, based on typical multisensory integration benefits",
    "ICMS Only may outperform visual-only conditions in dim environments, while Bright Visual Only may approach Combined performance",
    "Sham condition expected to show poorest performance (highest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, highest AD indicating more erratic paths)",
    "Path Efficiency and AD likely inversely related, with efficient paths showing low angular dispersion",
    "Multinomial logistic regression expected to achieve moderate-to-good classification accuracy (>60%), with strongest discrimination between Sham and Combined conditions",
    "Dim Visual Only and Bright Visual Only may be difficult to distinguish from each other based on performance metrics alone"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance in Stim Paradigm (Combined 63.7% vs. Bright Visual Only 4.3%) will reduce statistical power for rare conditions and bias predictive models toward majority class",
    "Crossed random effects not identifiable (only Mouse as clustering variable, no Session or Day information)",
    "No information on trial order, learning effects, or fatigue across the 76655 trials",
    "AD maximum of 1.0 suggests possible censoring or boundary effects for angular dispersion",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme maximum (29.8) suggesting outliers or calculation artifacts that may violate normality",
    "Temperature=0.0 in run metadata suggests deterministic LLM generation, but unclear if this affects data collection or analysis protocol",
    "Single replication (Run ID 142, Replication 2) limits generalizability; no estimate of between-replication variance",
    "No covariates for difficulty, target location, or environmental conditions beyond stimulation paradigm"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a linear mixed-effects model with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect for each continuous outcome, followed by estimated marginal means with Tukey adjustment; for Success, use generalized linear mixed model with binomial family; then fit multinomial logistic regression with 5-fold stratified cross-validation to predict Stim Paradigm from standardized performance variables, reporting per-class precision/recall and confusion matrix to address class imbalance"
}
